verdict.rationale: Name.com lets users issue separate development and production API tokens (name-com-docs-22) and authenticates via API credentials (name-com-docs-1), but there is no evidence of granular scopes, permission levels, or least-privilege roles (e.g., read-only vs. write, per-domain restrictions) that would let an AI agent be issued a truly least-privilege credential. The MCP server (name-com-docs-9) uses these same undifferentiated credentials rather than a scoped token. Missing for 10: documented scope/permission granularity, role-based or read-only token types, and evidence that agent credentials can be restricted to specific operations or domains.
